criterion_notes.c1: Focuses on project management models in the formulation and execution of rural drinking water and basic sanitation projects in Aguazul, Casanare, rather than directly measuring household or community water/sanitation service access (apart from one general perception question in a 20-person survey asking whether projects satisfy the needs of the whole community).
criterion_notes.c2: PASSES PLAIN WORDING ONLY SUPERFICIALLY / FAILS NARROW 2026-10-13 READING: Under the plain literal wording of Criterion 2, evaluating municipal, departmental, and regional project-management models and checking whether project design files incorporated technical regulations (RAS 2000), legal analysis, governance, public-private financing, and citizen participation could be construed broadly as examining an institutional/administrative factor (though even under the plain reading the paper would still be excluded overall for lacking a service-access outcome under Criterion 4). Under the active 2026-10-13 narrow rule-type reading, Criterion 2 is strictly 'no' because the paper evaluates generic PMI-style project delivery and project-formulation checklist parameters (formulation, planning, execution, control, closure) rather than a rule-type mechanism directly governing household or community service access (such as eligibility screening, administrative burden, documentation or tenure requirements, tariff/cost-recovery rules, discretion/accommodation, enforcement, or utility ownership/regulatory structure governing access).
criterion_notes.c3: Contains primary descriptive empirical data consisting of a document review/validation of 14 planning variables across 42 formulated and executed rural water and sanitation project reports (selected from 212 projects listed in Table 2 / 200 stated in the Abstract) and a 10-question descriptive survey of 20 rural community respondents.
criterion_notes.c4: No household or community service-access outcome (access, connection, availability, reliability/continuity, quantity, affordability, or exclusion) is measured. Table 4 reports only whether project reports included 14 planning variables at the design stage (e.g., whether coverage censuses, GIS, RAS 2000, or citizen participation were considered during project formulation), and Table 5 reports perceptions of pre-project consultation/training plus a single unspecific item on whether projects satisfy the needs of the whole community (20% yes, 80% no).
criterion_notes.c5: Units of analysis are split between 42 project documents and an uncharacterized sample of 20 survey respondents without sampling details, and no identifiable exposure-to-service-access-outcome relationship is specified.
criterion_notes.c6: Full text is in Spanish with an English title and abstract. Although Spanish is not among the languages eligible without translation under Criterion 9 (English, Portuguese, Dutch), assessment/translation directly from the provided Spanish full text is feasible per Criterion 10.

evidence_quotes.quote: This research evaluated the management models of rural drinking water and basic sanitation projects. 200 projects were collected from the governorate, mayor and regional environmental authority. 42 projects formulated and executed were selected, they were used as input to carry out an integral qualitative analysis of 14 variables.

La Gestión de Proyectos es un enfoque metódico para planificar y orientar los procesos del proyecto de principio a fin. Según el Instituto de Gestión de Proyectos (PMI), los procesos se guían por cinco etapas: formulación (diseño), planificación, ejecución, control y cierre [11].

Después de obtener las variables, saber su significado y aplicabilidad, se realizó una revisión en cada uno de los informes de proyectos formulados y ejecutados validando si se utilizaron estas variables al momento de su diseño, esta validación se realizó en una muestra de 42 proyectos.
Finalmente se diseñó una encuesta la cual se le aplico a una muestra de comunidades rurales que se definió estadísticamente realizando un análisis descriptivo.

En la encuesta realizada a comunidades del área rural del municipio de aguazul Casanare, se encontró que la percepción de la comunidad es que no se tienen en cuenta al momento de ser formulados los proyectos, ellos como usuarios y son los que tienen identificadas las necesidades que tienen deberían ser más vinculados ya que ellos pueden brindar una información más clara y precisa de algunas variables como lo es la cobertura.

raw_response.exposure: Project management models and inclusion of 14 planning/design parameters in rural water and sanitation project formulation reports
raw_response.outcome: Project-design compliance with 14 planning variables (Table 4) and descriptive community survey responses on pre-project consultation, participation, training, and general satisfaction of community needs (Table 5)
raw_response.population_and_sample: 42 formulated and executed rural drinking water and basic sanitation project reports (from 212 listed in Table 2 / 200 in Abstract) from regional, departmental, and municipal authorities in Aguazul, Casanare, plus 20 rural survey respondents
raw_response.rationale: Excluded primarily under E03 (Wrong exposure) and secondarily lacking an eligible access outcome (c4). The study evaluates generic PMI-style project management and project-formulation practices across 42 rural drinking water and basic sanitation project documents in Aguazul, Casanare, Colombia, alongside a 20-person descriptive survey on community consultation during project formulation. Under the 2026-10-13 Criterion 2 clarification, generic project delivery and project-design checklist compliance (whether formulation documents considered GIS, RAS 2000 technical standards, censuses, or citizen participation) do not constitute a rule-type legal, regulatory, or administrative mechanism directly governing household or community service access. Even under the plain broad wording of Criterion 2, the study would still be excluded because it measures project-document design compliance and consultation perceptions rather than any concrete water or sanitation access, connection, availability, reliability, quantity, affordability, or exclusion outcome (Criterion 4).
raw_response.study_design: Descriptive diagnostic study (cross-sectional audit of 42 project reports and descriptive survey of 20 rural community members)
